message.content:
The most commonly cited figure for California’s residential real‑estate market is the **median home price** (the middle value when all home prices are sorted). As of the latest data from Zillow (Q4 2023) and the U.S. Census Bureau’s American Community Survey, the median home value in California is roughly **$800,000–$850,000**.

If you’re looking for an *average* (mean) price rather than the median, the figure is a bit higher because a handful of very expensive homes pull the mean up. Recent estimates put the mean home price in California at about **$900,000–$950,000**.

**Key points**

| Metric | Approximate Value | Notes |
|--------|-------------------|-------|
| Median home price (2023) | $800k–$850k | Most widely reported; less sensitive to outliers |
| Mean (average) home price (2023) | $900k–$950k | Higher due to luxury properties |
| Source | Zillow Home Value Index, U.S. Census ACS | Data updated quarterly |

These numbers are rounded and can vary slightly depending on the exact methodology and the time of year. If you need the most current figure, check Zillow’s “Home Value Index” or the U.S. Census Bureau’s latest ACS release.
